assessments.label: Molecular cause and pathogenesis
assessments.objective: Connect disease-driving pathology to candidate's therapeutic target
assessments.failureMechanism: Mechanistic mismatch could undercut causal plausibility
assessments.requiredSources: Disease natural-history publications; biomarker validation; FDA disease reviews

assessments.label: Untreated progression and variability
assessments.objective: Quantify untreated progression, spontaneous remission, measurement variability and prognosis
assessments.failureMechanism: Natural history could explain apparent response or weaken endpoint sensitivity
assessments.requiredSources: Longitudinal cohorts; registries; natural-history analyses

assessments.label: Disease biomarkers and surrogate validity
assessments.objective: Examine biomarker analytical validity, clinical meaning and surrogate qualification
assessments.failureMechanism: A surrogate may not reliably predict patient benefit
assessments.requiredSources: FDA endpoint guidance; biomarker validation; clinical-outcome correlations

assessments.label: Current treatment burden and unmet need
assessments.objective: Define therapeutic baseline and patient-important outcomes for indication
assessments.failureMechanism: Benefit-risk context may not justify tolerability burden
assessments.requiredSources: Approved labels; guidelines; patient studies; comparative data

assessments.label: Diagnostic and population heterogeneity
assessments.objective: Assess diagnostic error, organ severity, genetic, demographic and responder subtypes
assessments.failureMechanism: Misclassification or restricted efficacy may limit proposed indication
assessments.requiredSources: Eligibility criteria; genotypes; baseline subgroups; diagnostic publications

assessments.label: Drug target validation
assessments.objective: Trace target specificity and causal importance in disease biology
assessments.failureMechanism: Target is noncausal or poorly validated
assessments.requiredSources: Target genetics; target perturbation; structural and molecular biology

assessments.label: Mechanism of action and target engagement
assessments.objective: Validate engagement, tissue penetration, occupancy, and downstream activity
assessments.failureMechanism: Exposure may not reach relevant tissue or achieve the proposed mechanism
assessments.requiredSources: In-vitro/in-vivo target assays; human biomarkers; PK/PD

assessments.label: Selectivity and off-target liabilities
assessments.objective: Assess selectivity, unintended pathways and differential tissue safety
assessments.failureMechanism: Off-target toxicity may offset observed efficacy
assessments.requiredSources: Off-target panels; safety pharmacology; exposure margins

assessments.label: Systems/pathway feedback and compensation
assessments.objective: Model cross-pathway effects, feedback and alternative causal hypotheses
assessments.failureMechanism: Compensatory biology may blunt durable effect or increase risk
assessments.requiredSources: Pathway experiments; omics; resistant phenotypes

assessments.label: Resistance and loss of response
assessments.objective: Examine target escape, neutralizing antibodies, tolerance and durability
assessments.failureMechanism: Loss of action could undermine long-term benefit
assessments.requiredSources: Resistance mechanism studies; repeat-dosing clinical follow-up

assessments.label: Cellular potency and reproducibility
assessments.objective: Assess preclinical assays, controls, batch-to-batch reliability
assessments.failureMechanism: Assay artifacts or inconsistent product potency
assessments.requiredSources: Cell-line assays; potency validation; SOPs

assessments.label: Animal models and model fitness
assessments.objective: Test construct, external and translational validity of animal models
assessments.failureMechanism: Nonpredictive models can exaggerate expected benefit
assessments.requiredSources: Animal model datasets; species differences

assessments.label: Human PK/PD and exposure–response
assessments.objective: Compare dose, exposure, target saturation, exposure-efficacy and exposure-safety
assessments.failureMechanism: Inadequate dose selection or pharmacology evidence
assessments.requiredSources: Population PK; dose-ranging; model diagnostics

assessments.label: Nonclinical toxicology and margins
assessments.objective: Assess carcinogenicity, reproductive safety, chronic toxicity and organ-risk margins as applicable
assessments.failureMechanism: Unresolved nonclinical risks may restrict approval/label
assessments.requiredSources: GLP toxicology; exposure multiples; toxicology reviews

assessments.label: Cross-stage translational coherence
assessments.objective: Trace changes in mechanism, effect size, dose and biomarker from early to pivotal trials
assessments.failureMechanism: Phase-to-phase inconsistency may reflect model fragility
assessments.requiredSources: Phase 1–3 protocols; cross-study estimates

assessments.label: Randomization, blinding and comparator
assessments.objective: Evaluate randomization, concealment, masking, site conduct and control appropriateness
assessments.failureMechanism: Bias or invalid comparator can invalidate efficacy evidence
assessments.requiredSources: Protocol; CONSORT; monitoring; regulatory correspondence

assessments.label: Endpoint selection and clinical meaning
assessments.objective: Reconstruct endpoint definitions, validation, hierarchy and change dates
assessments.failureMechanism: Unacceptable endpoint or clinically marginal effect
assessments.requiredSources: Original/final protocol; endpoint charter; FDA guidance

assessments.label: Estimands, intercurrent events and missingness
assessments.objective: Match estimand to treatment-policy/hypothetical/composite strategy; test missingness
assessments.failureMechanism: Selective censoring/imputation can reverse the outcome
assessments.requiredSources: Original SAP; final SAP; CSR; raw-data sensitivity analyses

assessments.label: Population, allocation and statistical power
assessments.objective: Review target population, sample size, subgroup power, eligibility and attrition
assessments.failureMechanism: Underpowered/misaligned population can invalidate claim
assessments.requiredSources: Enrollment; eligibility; power assumptions; trial registry

assessments.label: Conduct, deviations and data integrity
assessments.objective: Examine sites, protocol changes, adjudication, withdrawals and inspections
assessments.failureMechanism: Data or conduct findings may trigger FDA objections
assessments.requiredSources: Deviation logs; inspections; protocol amendments; audit reports

assessments.label: Pivotal primary efficacy
assessments.objective: Compare prespecified primary treatment effect, CI, p and clinical effect thresholds
assessments.failureMechanism: Primary failure may directly prevent approval
assessments.requiredSources: Full primary results; locked SAP; FDA reviewer tables

assessments.label: Secondary endpoints, multiplicity and hierarchy
assessments.objective: Check testing sequence, adjustment and label-claim boundaries
assessments.failureMechanism: Nominal or post-hoc endpoints cannot rescue a failed primary without strong context
assessments.requiredSources: SAP multiplicity plan; alpha spending; FDA multiple endpoints

assessments.label: Integrated safety and competing harms
assessments.objective: Analyze serious AEs, death, organ toxicity, rates, time at risk and causality
assessments.failureMechanism: Benefit-risk may be unfavorable or require restrictions
assessments.requiredSources: Pooled safety; SAE line lists; lab shifts; label precedents

assessments.label: Subgroups, effect modification and robustness
assessments.objective: Test true treatment–subgroup interaction, missingness and consistency
assessments.failureMechanism: Apparent overall effect may not generalize to label
assessments.requiredSources: Interaction CIs; baseline balance; multiplicity controls

assessments.label: Replication, durability and long-term effects
assessments.objective: Assess study-to-study consistency, external validation and attrition of follow-up
assessments.failureMechanism: Transient efficacy or non-reproducibility could limit approval
assessments.requiredSources: Separate randomized trials; OLE limits; long-term outcomes

assessments.label: Current standard-of-care performance
assessments.objective: Establish relevant comparator and expected patient outcomes
assessments.failureMechanism: Misleading placebo-only or historical comparison
assessments.requiredSources: Current guidelines; approved labels; direct trials

assessments.label: Competing assets and alternatives
assessments.objective: Compare efficacy, safety and stage-matched populations without invalid cross-trial claims
assessments.failureMechanism: Indirect comparison may overstate differentiating benefits
assessments.requiredSources: Head-to-head trials; network meta-analysis (when valid)

assessments.label: Class effects and precedent failures
assessments.objective: Examine class-wide efficacy, severe events and regulatory warnings
assessments.failureMechanism: Shared mechanism may import risk not seen in small studies
assessments.requiredSources: Labels; safety surveillance; historical CRLs

assessments.label: Clinically meaningful differentiation
assessments.objective: Quantify NNT/NNH, PROs, dosing burden and practical utility where valid
assessments.failureMechanism: Marginal incremental benefit might not offset risk
assessments.requiredSources: Patient preferences; comparative outcomes; exposure

assessments.label: Combination therapy and sequencing
assessments.objective: Analyze interaction, additive harms, pharmacology, and role in therapy
assessments.failureMechanism: Drug interactions or positioning weaknesses may affect label
assessments.requiredSources: Combination trials; DDI; sequencing evidence

assessments.label: Application and review-cycle identity
assessments.objective: Verify NDA/BLA/supplement, indication, pathways, goal and prior action letters
assessments.failureMechanism: Wrong cycle or unaccepted filing makes prediction invalid
assessments.requiredSources: FDA records; dated SEC documents; approval/CRL history

assessments.label: FDA communications and prior objections
assessments.objective: Trace agency comments, prior deficiencies and applicant remediation
assessments.failureMechanism: Unresolved stated FDA concern may trigger CRL
assessments.requiredSources: FDA advisory package; letters when public; meeting minutes

assessments.label: Label, population, endpoint and indication fit
assessments.objective: Compare requested claim against studied population and supported clinical benefit
assessments.failureMechanism: Unsupported indication or claim may be rejected or narrowed
assessments.requiredSources: Proposed/approved labeling; endpoints; FDA precedent

assessments.label: REMS, safety management and inspections
assessments.objective: Examine tolerability, REMS, pharmacovigilance, BIMO and inspection findings
assessments.failureMechanism: Unresolved safety or inspection problems may prevent approval
assessments.requiredSources: Public inspection records; risk controls; safety reviews

assessments.label: CMC, facilities, stability and major amendment timing
assessments.objective: Assess process control, identity/purity/potency, facility status and amendments
assessments.failureMechanism: Unresolved quality deficiency may cause CRL; major amendment may extend clock
assessments.requiredSources: CMC disclosures; inspections; validation; PDUFA goals

assessments.label: Integrated clinical benefit-risk
assessments.objective: Integrate magnitude, uncertainty, severity, treatment options, safety tradeoffs
assessments.failureMechanism: Insufficient evidence of favorable benefit-risk
assessments.requiredSources: Full trial/regulator evidence matrix; disease context

assessments.label: Contradictions and missing-data map
assessments.objective: Audit discrepancies between FDA, publications, SEC releases and trial registry
assessments.failureMechanism: Unresolved contradictions erode reproducibility and FDA-readiness
assessments.requiredSources: Dated comparative sources; original document sections

assessments.label: CRL, delay and withdrawal pathways
assessments.objective: Build separate causal routes for efficacy, safety, CMC, integrity and timing
assessments.failureMechanism: Failure modes may be missed if focus only on positive top-line
assessments.requiredSources: Historical CRLs; active FDA concerns; PDUFA procedures

assessments.label: Real-world effectiveness, external validity and label restrictions
assessments.objective: Assess transportability, dose burden, population and health-system factors
assessments.failureMechanism: Limited external validity may shrink intended label
assessments.requiredSources: Representative cohorts; subgroup confidence; real-world records

assessments.label: Independent scientific judgment and reversal conditions
assessments.objective: Red-team all claims, test counterfactuals, document strongest objection and what changes judgment
assessments.failureMechanism: Overconfidence or hidden assumptions produce false forecasts
assessments.requiredSources: Independent sourced challenge, replication audit, calibrated historic outcomes

methods.name: Document extraction and source authentication
methods.method: Authenticate dated original protocol/SAP, clinical/FDA documents and every factual claim
methods.deliverable: Source ledger with precise references, date and version

methods.name: Scientific hypothesis reconstruction
methods.method: Translate the candidate mechanism into falsifiable medical expectations

methods.name: Biological plausibility investigation
methods.method: Trace molecular and organ-level mechanisms and biological alternatives

methods.name: Evidence quality validation
methods.method: Audit study methods, measurements, provenance and quality

methods.name: Critical challenge
methods.method: Seek primary contradictions, biases and alternative explanations

methods.name: Cross-disciplinary integration
methods.method: Compare disease biology, pharmacology, clinical design and regulation

methods.name: Predictive scenario modeling
methods.method: Define approval/CRL/delay counterfactuals; never fabricate probabilities

methods.name: Scientific synthesis
methods.method: Distinguish supported, mixed and unsupported evidence

methods.name: Causal inference
methods.method: Assess what observations can truly establish drug-caused benefit
methods.deliverable: Causal graph, confounding and identification limits

methods.name: Systems biology
methods.method: Examine feedback networks, compensation and systemic off-target pathways

methods.name: Adversarial scientific review
methods.method: Actively disprove strongest favorable conclusion

methods.name: Multi-method adjudication
methods.method: Reconcile prespecified, FDA, company, alternative and sensitivity estimates

methods.name: Quantitative pharmacology
methods.method: Evaluate dose/exposure/response/target engagement when data permit

methods.name: Patient heterogeneity
methods.method: Test interaction, population transportability and biomarker-specific outcomes

methods.name: Bayesian evidence integration
methods.method: Update uncertainty only with defendable priors/data; avoid false posterior precision
methods.deliverable: Transparent prior, likelihood and sensitivity if feasible

methods.name: External validity
methods.method: Compare trial patients, delivery setting and outcomes to labeled use

methods.name: Historical failure patterns
methods.method: Find similar FDA CRLs and identify genuine versus superficial analogies

methods.name: Regulatory counterfactuals
methods.method: Simulate scientifically plausible FDA reviewer interpretations and alternative labeling

methods.name: Independent reproducibility audit
methods.method: Reproduce equations, effect metrics and p-values only with sufficient inputs

methods.name: Final red-team adjudication
methods.method: Force independent opposition and scientific judgment with decision-reversal triggers
methods.deliverable: Adjudicated evidence state and unresolved blockers

EARLY_PHASE1.question: Dose escalation, exposure and target engagement adequate?
Any dose-limiting or serious emergent toxicity?
First-in-human enrollment and monitoring proceeding as planned?

PHASE1.question: Therapeutic exposure and maximum tolerated or selected dose supported?
Any serious adverse events, DLTs, discontinuations or immunogenicity?
Are any early signals controlled and interpretable rather than assumed efficacy?

PHASE2.question: Magnitude and repeatability of preliminary benefit versus control?
Endpoint validity, missing data, multiplicity and underpowered findings?
Dose-selection and exposure-response evidence support pivotal planning?
Toxicity profile and duration adequate for Phase 3 advancement?

PHASE3.question: Prespecified primary endpoint and clinically meaningful effect achieved, when reported?
Multiplicity, amendments, missingness, prespecified versus post-hoc estimates?
Enrollment, retention, blinding and site/data integrity risks?
Serious harms, exposure and benefit-risk consistency?
FDA endpoints and evidence requirements resolved for the exact indication?

PHASE4.question: New or cumulative rare/long-term safety signals?
Postmarketing commitments and confirmatory results on track?
Effectiveness across populations and care settings?

UNKNOWN.question: Confirm exact-NCT trial phase before assessing current-phase risk.
